Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

logconNMF 0.1.0.9000

  • Corrected the historical one-unit mass-axis offset in gcmsData1: the all-zero leading channel was removed and the retained channels now have their nominal labels, m/z 30:699. gcmsData2 was independently checked against its source CDF and required no correction.

PSF estimation and deconvolution

  • convKernel(), shiftKernel() and convMatrix() construct PSFs and convolution designs, including asymmetric bigaussian and EMG responses.
  • estimatePSF() estimates constant or smoothly time-varying point spread functions from standards or overlapping signals and returns a sparse design.
  • Alternating spike-train and kernel estimation supports single or multiple channels, smooth backgrounds and information-criterion checkpoints.

Sparse log-concave matrix factorization

  • logconNMF() estimates nonnegative profiles and loadings with hard log-concavity constraints and automatic best rank tuning.
  • Local profile, spectrum and background updates, algebraic candidate fusion, conditional deletion and residual additions use original-channel criteria.
  • Native profile fits use banded Cholesky systems with residual checks, iterative correction and a rank-revealing fallback. Cached local workspaces and continued active sets accelerate profile, spectral and background fits.
  • Gaussian, Poisson, quasipoisson, NB2, NB1, censored Gamma and common-scale Gamma models, with pooled noise calibration and optional temporal adjustment.
  • Optional channel aggregation accelerates initialization; final refinement retains every original outcome channel.
  • Permissive initialization and native fine-scale profile/spectrum refinement preserve candidate components for final correlation-aware rank selection.
  • Likelihood-checked local width restarts resolve signal allocation between nearly coincident profiles. Screening and acceptance retain all original channels and compare with an equally refined control.
  • Contained broad-peak fragments are compared with equally refined unmerged controls. Complete local supports, reconstructed original-channel means and separate initialization/final-criterion ledgers make each decision auditable.

Simultaneous multisample models

  • logconNMF() with a sample list shares spectra across samples with sample-specific profiles, areas and backgrounds, allowing compounds to be absent from individual samples.

  • Monotone alignment, area-ordered profile compatibility and exposure-aware likelihoods retain each sample’s original irregular scan grid.

  • Disk-backed observations, batched native spectral scores, shared row inputs, sparse profiles and OpenMP support efficient fitting.

  • A total logical-core budget schedules independent fits and simultaneous sample updates concurrently, with deterministic spectral reductions and restored BLAS settings. Native block reads retain bounded original-channel buffers.

  • Common saved channel maps, a compact aggregate cache and full-channel acceptance checks support reusable, memory-efficient multisample analyses.

  • Incremental fusion candidates retain the same greedy order while refreshing only edges affected by a merge.

Simulation and interpretation

  • Single- and multisample simulations include drifting retention times, concentration-dependent width/tailing, broad profiles and missing compounds.
  • Optional retention-index calibration places reference spectra along the chromatogram. Concentration-dependent broadening preserves leading edges, and each sample records its generating retention-time–RI map.
  • Simulation baselines can be supplied as common levels, channel-specific intensities or smooth reference matrices on the original intensity scale.
  • Experimental multichannel signals, profile and spectral plots, factor extraction, likelihood and information-criterion methods.
  • Tutorials follow PSF estimation, single-sample factorization and simultaneous factorization; a separate mathematical article gives objectives and pseudocode.
